newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close day lower, account with gain.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close day lower, account with gain.

text.p: French shares closed lower on Monday along with other markets, among which was an early 50-point fall in the Dow Jones Index, on fears that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will raise U.S. rates on Tuesday.
The French fall was also due to profit-taking on the last day of the September account, which ended with a 2.29 percent gain. The market has gained 10.42 percent since December 31.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 12.37 points or 0.59 percent at 2,067.09, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 10.5 at 2,072. Volume was a modest 3.05 billion francs, of which two billion in CAC-40 stocks.
A small majority of financial analysts is expecting the FOMC to raise Fed funds by 0.25 points on Tuesday.
"If the Fed raised its rates by 25 basis points then you can say that it is already in the price. If it raised by as much as 50 points, then prices will fall," a dealer said.
Investors were sidelined ahead of the FOMC meeting as well as a series of important corporate results due this week, including Alcatel, LVMH, Lafarge, Canal Plus and AXA.
* Peugeot closed 2.4 percent down at 569 francs after reporting a drop in first half results.

PSA Peugeot Citroen said its profit for the first six months of 1996 shrank by more than half as a brutal price war in France took a heavy toll on the domestic car industry. Net attributable profit fell to 602 million francs from 1.22 billion, and its operating margin shrank to 1.34 billion francs from 2.78 billion. "It's a good company in a terrible environment, and right now, the environment is more important," one analyst said.

* Canal Plus slipped 0.33 percent to 1,191 francs after a rise on Friday on the back of a early morning block trade of 1.33 percent of its capital. Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), a shareholder in Luxembourg's CLT, emerged as the buyer.

Canal Plus is set to report its first half results on Tuesday after market closing. Brokers Oddo see a 19 percent rise to 394 million francs, but more important will be what the company says about the expected negative impact on short term earnings from its planned merger with Nethold.

* Alcatel, down 0.08 percent to 388.70 franc, will publish its results on Thursday and analysts expect a loss of at least 500 million francs and perhaps as much as 1.5 billion. But there too the actual result is not the most important figure and analysts will be looking at the operating level, with Alcatel set to provide a divisional break-down at the first-half stage.
* Pernod-Ricard gains 0.29 percent to 279.10 francs after it confirms it is studying a share buy-back programme. Pernod lost a lot of ground last week on disappointing first half results.

* The French government launched a tender last week to appoint a bank adviser for the sale of shares in its minority holdings, business daily l'Agefi said on Monday. Its Elf Aquitaine and Renault stakes are not among the stakes, the report said. The holdings to be sold include Pechiney, Usinor Sacilor, Credit Local de France, Seita and Roussel-Uclaf.
Other stakes include Rhone-Poulenc, Union des Assurances de Paris (, Banque Nationale de Paris, and Assurances Generales de France.
* The French public sector unions called for a one-day strike and demonstration on October 17 to protest against expected job cuts resulting from the 1997 budget.
* The franc posted gains on Monday after the Dublin summit of European finance ministers on monetary union.
